name: Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016)

criteria.description: Expression of specific markers of more than one hematopoietic lineage (myeloid, B-lymphoid, or T-lymphoid) on leukemic blasts
Presence of ≥20% blasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Exclusion of other defined acute leukemias such as AML with recurrent genetic abnormalities or ALL

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ≥20% blasts with expression of markers from at least two distinct hematopoietic lineages, excluding other defined acute leukemias
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Immunophenotyping by flow cytometry is essential; cytogenetic and molecular studies assist in classification and prognosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Presence of blasts expressing markers of multiple lineages
searchTerms: immature white blood cells in blood
presence of leukemic blasts in circulation
bone marrow not producing enough blood cells
failure to make red, white cells and platelets
pale skin and tiredness from anemia
fatigue and pallor due to low red blood cells
recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells

common.symptomName: Easy bruising or bleeding from thrombocytopenia

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion

searchTerms: losing weight and sweating at night

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement

rare.symptomName: Chloroma (myeloid sarcoma) presenting as extramedullary mass

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing blasts with mixed lineage markers
Bone marrow biopsy with ≥20% blasts expressing myeloid and lymphoid markers
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT may show mediastinal lymphadenopathy
MRI or CT for CNS involvement if neurological symptoms present
genetic: Cytogenetic abnormalities including t(9;22)(q34;q11) BCR-ABL1 fusion in some cases
other: Flow cytometry immunophenotyping essential for lineage assignment

distinguishingFeatures: Blasts express predominantly myeloid markers only
Absence of significant lymphoid marker expression
Blasts express predominantly B- or T-lymphoid markers only
No co-expression of myeloid markers meeting MPAL criteria
Dysplastic changes in marrow without ≥20% blasts

redFlags: Rapid onset of pancytopenia with circulating blasts
Extramedullary masses or CNS symptoms indicating leukemic infiltration
Poor response to standard AML or ALL chemotherapy protocols
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Swerdlow SH, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
